evidence: waits: Table_SoundDrv_Durations[opcode-$80]-1 goes into track+1 and the next command is read on the tick that finds the counter 0; it produces no silence (a note never comes here), so the old name was misleading (docs/research/audio_format.md section 9); tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): note duration/gate and wait checks

runs once per tick for every track (end of SoundDrv_StepTrack, also after a wait starts): track+$2B delay counter, triangle LFO phase track+$20 += rate track+$1F, depth track+$21+$22, output word track+$24/$25 (skipped while track+$23 != 0), then falls into SoundDrv_ComputeTrackOutput; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model) reproduces the period series of 6 settings exactly

opcode $BD: stores the stream byte in track+$12 (ld bc,$0012 ; jp $4973), added to the pitch byte at every note start; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): $0C raises the period table index by 12 (an octave), $F4 lowers it by 12

entry 1 of Table_SoundDrv_ParamHandlers: writes the word (D038/D039) to track+$13/$14 of the selected tracks and sets their flag bit 2; SoundDrv_ComputeTrackOutput adds that word to the pitch offset; probe on the running driver: word $0100 moves pulse 2 from period $672 to $689 (+1 semitone)

opcode $C1: track+$19 = 2*byte-$80, track+$1B/$1C = signed (2*track+$19) * track+$1A (scale), flag bit 2 (pitch); pitch offset (byte-$40)*scale/64 semitones; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): 60 (value, scale) combinations equal the model

shared by $C1 and $C2: b = signed bend, c = scale, Mul8x8, sign handling, result word to track+$1B/$1C, sets flag bit 2; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model)

opcode $C2: stores the byte in track+$1A (2 at start) and recomputes the product of $C1; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): scale 0/1/2/4/8 give the modelled periods

opcode $C3: stores the byte in track+$1F (LFO phase step per tick, $17 at start); a byte of $00 or $80 also presets the phase track+$20 to $40 / $00; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model) (vibrato series)

entry 5 of Table_SoundDrv_ParamHandlers: the same track+$1F (vibrato rate) as opcode $C3 for the selected tracks; probe on the running driver: the value (D039) replaces track+$1F ($17 -> $30 in the record) and the vibrato period series changes

opcode $C4: stores the byte in track+$2A; every note start copies it to track+$2B, which SoundDrv_TickVibrato counts down while holding the phase; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): delay 3 and 10 give the modelled series (vibrato starts after the delay)

opcode $C0: flag bit 0 set, track+$17 = 2*byte-$80; SoundDrv_ComputeTrackOutput adds track+$18 into track+$2E, SoundDrv_WriteChannelPan masks the channel bits of NR51 by its bits 7/6; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): 32 values give left only < $20, both, right only >= $60
entry 3 of Table_SoundDrv_ParamHandlers: byte (D039) to track+$18 of the selected tracks, flag bit 0; probe on the running driver: $00 -> NR51 $FF, $80 -> NR51 $FD (pulse 2 left only)

opcode $C5: stores the byte in track+$21 (vibrato depth, 0 at start; peak-to-peak deviation depth*8/256 semitones, plus track+$22); tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model) (vibrato series)

common tail of the one-byte commands: stores the stream byte (wSoundDrv_StreamByte) at track+BC (BC = the offset the caller loaded), inc de, continues with the next command; users: $BD, $C4, $C5, $C6, $CA and the $CD sub-commands 1, 6, 7, 10, 11

opcode $C6: flag bits 0-2 set, stream byte to track+$23; while it is nonzero SoundDrv_ComputeTrackOutput leaves the vibrato word out of the pitch and SoundDrv_TickVibrato stops updating it; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): $C6 $01 freezes a vibrato note

entry 4 of Table_SoundDrv_ParamHandlers: byte (D039) to track+$22, the second addend of the vibrato depth (track+$21 + track+$22); probe on the running driver: track+$22 set to $40 on a vibrato note of depth $20, the period swing grows from 22 to 37 units

opcode $C9: flag bit 2, track+$1D = 2*byte-$80 (via SoundDrv_CmdStoreTrackSigned); SoundDrv_ComputeTrackOutput adds 2*that to the pitch offset: (byte-$40)/64 semitones; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): 6 values equal the model
stores rotl(stream byte)-$80 at track+BC (BC from the caller: $17 for $C0, $1D for $C9) and continues with the next command

idea: SoundDrv_CmdStoreTrack1E | opcode $CA: flag bit 2, stream byte to track+$1E; the byte is read nowhere (static review and a read watch in tools/audio_driver_check.py), so the effect is not demonstrated and the name stays neutral

$CD sub-command 6: stream byte to track+$27 (ld bc,$0027 ; jr $4973); the field is read at 04:4D67 when a note has run out; with sub 6/7 set, the driver was observed to re-trigger the channel at the note end (NR22 $40/$70 instead of the silencing $08); meaning of the field only partly demonstrated
$CD sub-command 7: stream byte to track+$28 (ld bc,$0028 ; jr $4973); read at 04:4D69 (the same note-end path); see SoundDrv_ExtSetTrack27
idea: SoundDrv_ParamTrackWord27 | entry 6 of Table_SoundDrv_ParamHandlers: word (D038/D039) to track+$27/$28 of the selected tracks; same fields as $CD sub 6/7; effect only partly demonstrated

$CD sub-command 1: stream byte to track+$0C = byte 0 of the instrument copy (channel class, duty/wave/width); tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): sub 1 changes the duty of the next pulse-2 note

$CD sub-command 10: stream byte to track+$0D = byte 1 of the instrument copy (length); tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): sub 10 sets the length bits of NR21 and bit 6 of NR24
$CD sub-command 11: stream byte to track+$0E = byte 2 of the instrument copy (NR10 sweep for pulse 1); code reading only, no probe

$CD sub-command 2: high nibble of track+$0F = byte 3 of the instrument copy; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): sub 2/3 together produce the attack write of byte 3 $A3
sets the high nibble of the byte at track+BC from the low nibble of the stream byte (swap, and $F0, or with the old low nibble); users: $CD sub 2 and 4
$CD sub-command 3: low nibble of track+$0F = byte 3 of the instrument copy; see SoundDrv_ExtSetInstrByte3Hi
sets the low nibble of the byte at track+BC from the stream byte (and $0F, or with the old high nibble); users: $CD sub 3 and 5
$CD sub-command 4: high nibble of track+$10 = byte 4 of the instrument copy (sustain field); code reading only, the probe checks only that the track runs on
$CD sub-command 5: low nibble of track+$10 = byte 4 of the instrument copy (release field); code reading only

jp SoundDrv_CmdEnd; the handler of the opcodes without a function ($B6-$B8, $C7, $C8, $CB) and of the $CD sub-commands 8 and 9; tools/audio_driver_check.py synthetic streams: each of them ends the track

opcode $CE: a note whose duration field is 0 (ld b,0 ; jr SoundDrv_ReadNoteBytes); with duration 0 SoundDrv_ServiceChannelGate never releases it, only sound_note_off ($CF) or the end of the track does; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): $CE/$CF check

shared by $CE and every note opcode: stores the duration in track+$0B, then reads the optional bytes (pitch $24-$7F to track+$09, volume $00-$1F to track+$0A as (v<<3)|7, adjust $20-$23 added to the duration) and falls into SoundDrv_StartNote; the synthetic note streams of tools/audio_driver_check.py (adjust bytes, byte order, duplicate classes, $CE) agree with the decoder

opcode $CF: optional pitch byte, then releases (SoundDrv_NoteGateExpired) each channel of this track that holds a note of that pitch with a zero gate counter; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): a held $CE note ends at the $CF with the same pitch (or none), not with another pitch

counts down the gate counter (channel+7 = the note duration) and releases the channel when it reaches 0 (falls into SoundDrv_NoteGateExpired); stops the channel when its track is gone; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): release at tick = duration for durations 3-40

hl -= 6 then falls into SoundDrv_StopChannel; reached by jr from SoundDrv_ServiceChannelGate and SoundDrv_UpdateChannel when the owning track has ended (track flags < $C0); never separated from the end-of-track behaviour observed in the synthetic songs
clears the channel flags at hl (channel inactive) and jumps to SoundDrv_SilenceChannel; every synthetic song of tools/audio_driver_check.py ends with this silencing write (NRx2 $08, NRx4 $80)
hl -= 5: a = channel byte 4 of the instrument copy & $F0 (the sustain field), hl += 5 again, z when the field is 0; used to end a note whose sustain level is 0

channel+$10 = (MulNibbles(track+$2F, channel+6 = note volume) + $0F) & $F0: the volume nibble the channel attacks to; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): 36 (track volume, note volume) combinations equal the model

channel+$10 = volume nibble of the sustain level: MulNibbles(track+$2F, MulNibbles(instrument byte 4, note volume) + $0F) + $0F, & $F0; tools/audio_driver_check.py (effects: whole frame tick on synthetic songs, APU writes compared with a model): the sustain write of instruments $00-$63 equals the model

only for the wave channel (SoundDrv channel register $1C): sets the volume-changed flag when the top two bits of the level changed (NR32 has a two-bit level); code reading only, wave-channel volume was not simulated
